chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, from Sahib al-Askar (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We are brought something, and it is said, 'This is what was for Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) with us.' So how should we deal with it?' He said: 'Whatever was for Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) by reason of the Imamate, it is for me; and whatever was other than that, it is an inheritance according to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir or Imam al-Sadiq depending on context, here referring to the predecessor)

ai.seo_question: How are the possessions of an Imam distributed between the current Imam and general inheritance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hadi (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinction between the personal wealth of the Imams and the specific assets acquired through their unique status as 'Imamate' (such as the Khums or gifts given specifically to the office). This ruling establishes that while general possessions follow standard inheritance laws, items tied to the Imamate are retained by the succeeding Imam, reflecting the continuity of spiritual and administrative authority in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Ali Bin Rashid, 
(It has been narrated) from Sahib Al-Askar<sup>asws</sup>,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! We are brought something, so it is said, ‘This is what was for Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> with us’. So how should we deal (with it)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whatever was for Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> by the cause of the Imamate, so it is for me<sup>asws</sup>, and whatever was other than that, so it is an inheritance upon the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and Sunnah of His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from abu Ali ibn Rashid who has narrated the following: “I once said to Sahib al- ‘Askar, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, something is brought to us and it is said “This is what was for abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam.” How must we deal with it?’

He (the Imam) said, ‘Whatever was for abu Ja‘far because of Imamat (leadership with divine authority), it belongs to me, and whatever is because of other reasons, it then is legacy according to the book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.’”
